title: General English   GCE Advanced Level Mock Paper
instructions: Answer all questions on this paper itself.
Marks will be deducted for bad punctuation (Omission of full stops, capital letters, etc.) and for mistakes in basic grammar.
The supervisor will provide you with sheets for rough work.

sections.title: PART A   GRAMMAR and VOCABULARY
sections.instructions: Answer all questions in this section related to Grammar and Vocabulary.

questions.prompt:
Fill in the blanks in the following text, using the prepositions given in the box. Use each preposition only once. There is one preposition extra.

Prepositions: on, for, from, at, with, to

The scientist worked tirelessly (1)_______ his research. He focused keenly (2)_______ the details. He needed to extract data (3)_______ a specific sample. He presented his findings (4)_______ the conference. His dedication was rewarded (5)_______ an award.

Fill in each blank with the correct form of the verb given within brackets.

Last night, as I (1) (walk) home, I (2) (see) a strange light in the sky. It (3) (move) very fast and then suddenly (4) (stop). I (5) (never/believe) in UFOs before, but this sight (6) (make) me wonder. When I (7) (reach) home, my neighbours (8) (discuss) the same thing. They (9) (already/call) the local observatory, which (10) (say) they (not/detect) anything unusual.

Underline the most appropriate word from those given within brackets to fill in the blanks in the following text.

The new eco-friendly project aims to (1) (reduce/ lessen/ decrease) plastic waste in our cities. Volunteers are encouraged to (2) (join/ attend/ participate) in the clean-up drives. Proper waste (3) (disposal/ disposition/ discard) is crucial for a (4) (healthy/ wholesome/ sound) environment. The local community has shown great (5) (support/ assistance/ help) for this initiative. They hope to (6) (create/ make/ build) a sustainable future. The government is also planning to (7) (launch/ initiate/ begin) new policies. These policies will (8) (promote/ encourage/ foster) responsible consumption. Everyone needs to (9) (contribute/ donate/ give) their part. This will (10) (ensure/ secure/ guarantee) a cleaner planet for generations to come.

Underline the correct word-ending, selecting from those given within brackets.

The (1) govern........... (ment/ mental/ mented) announced new policies to enhance (2) educ........... (ate/ ational/ ation) standards. These initiatives aim to foster (3) creat........... (ive/ ion/ ivity) thinking among students. Many believe this will lead to a more (4) produc........... (tivity/ tive/ tion) workforce. The long-term (5) bene........... (fit/ ficial/ fitment) for society is expected to be substantial.

questions.context_passage: The ancient city, once a thriving metropolis, now lies in ruins. Archaeologists are meticulously excavating the site to unravel its mysteries. They discovered intricate carvings, suggesting a sophisticated culture. Evidence points to a sudden decline, possibly due to environmental changes or conflict. Despite the challenges, their endeavor promises to shed light on a lost civilization.

sections.title: PART B   READING and WRITING
sections.instructions: Answer all questions in this section related to Reading and Writing.

questions.prompt: Underline the option that best expresses the meaning of each of the sentences given below in bold print.

sub_parts.prompt:
Despite the heavy rain, the children went out to play.
(a) The children stayed indoors because of the rain.
(b) The children played outside even though it was raining heavily.
(c) The rain stopped, so the children went to play.
(d) The children waited for the rain to stop before playing.

Had she known about the party, she would have attended.
(a) She knew about the party and attended it.
(b) She did not know about the party, so she did not attend.
(c) She did not attend the party even though she knew about it.
(d) She attended the party because she was informed.

It is no use crying over spilled milk.
(a) One should cry when milk spills.
(b) There's no point being upset about something that cannot be changed.
(c) Spilled milk is a serious problem.
(d) Crying helps solve problems.

The book is too expensive for me to buy.
(a) I can afford to buy the book.
(b) The book is not expensive, so I will buy it.
(c) The book is so expensive that I cannot buy it.
(d) I have enough money to buy the expensive book.

Unless you study hard, you will not pass the exam.
(a) You will pass the exam if you do not study hard.
(b) You will pass the exam even if you study hard.
(c) You need to study hard to pass the exam.
(d) Studying hard is not necessary to pass the exam.

questions.prompt:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

(I) Underline the most appropriate response in each of the questions from (1) - (5).

(II) Do the following statements agree with the information given in the above text? In boxes (6) - (10), write True, False or Not Given.

sub_parts.label: (I) (1)
sub_parts.prompt:
What is identified as an urgent global challenge?
(a) Population growth
(b) Climate change
(c) Economic recession
(d) Technological advancements

sub_parts.label: (I) (2)
sub_parts.prompt:
Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an impact of climate change?
(a) Rising global temperatures
(b) Increased biodiversity
(c) Extreme weather events
(d) Sea-level rise

sub_parts.label: (I) (3)
sub_parts.prompt:
What do scientists recommend for immediate action?
(a) Increasing fossil fuel production
(b) Reducing greenhouse gas emissions
(c) Expanding industrial activities
(d) Ignoring environmental warnings

sub_parts.label: (I) (4)
sub_parts.prompt:
Which individual effort is mentioned to combat climate change?
(a) Increasing personal consumption
(b) Advocating for policy changes
(c) Relying solely on government action
(d) Expanding carbon footprints

sub_parts.label: (I) (5)
sub_parts.prompt:
What additional factors are vital in mitigating climate change effects?
(a) Political instability
(b) International cooperation and technological innovations
(c) Increased deforestation
(d) Economic protectionism

sub_parts.label: (II) (6)
sub_parts.prompt: Climate change only affects developed countries.

sub_parts.label: (II) (7)
sub_parts.prompt: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions is a key step in addressing climate change.

sub_parts.label: (II) (8)
sub_parts.prompt: Individual actions have no significant impact on climate change.

sub_parts.label: (II) (9)
sub_parts.prompt: The passage suggests that technological innovations are not useful.

sub_parts.label: (II) (10)
sub_parts.prompt: Building a resilient future is a shared goal for the global community.

questions.context_passage: The global community faces an urgent challenge in combating climate change. Rising global temperatures, extreme weather events, and sea-level rise are becoming more frequent, impacting vulnerable populations disproportionately. Scientists warn that immediate and coordinated action is required to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition to renewable energy sources. Individual efforts, such as reducing carbon footprints, adopting sustainable consumption habits, and advocating for policy changes, are crucial. Additionally, international cooperation and technological innovations play a vital role in mitigating the adverse effects and building a resilient future for all.
